prize_parts.citation: for credible empirical analysis of how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, wages and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My names are unchanged from round 1, but my reasoning has shifted after the exchange. The achievement I would credit is measured evidence on how labour demand adjusts when trade and technology change. It rests on transparent local-labour-market designs for import competition (Autor, Dorn, Hanson), together with Autor's task-based account of why technology shifts demand across kinds of work. The designs have been replicated in several countries and refined without being overturned, and about a decade and a half of scrutiny means the live debate is over magnitude and persistence, not over whether adjustment costs are concentrated and long-lasting. The lesson is general and reaches well beyond labour economics. The narrower citation is deliberate. It claims the adjustment evidence and not the whole task or skill-premium framework, whose authorship extends to Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane. In round 1 I leaned heavily on overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes as the reason to prefer Dorn to Katz. Enflo, Fredriksson and Hjalmarsson persuaded me that this overlap is thematic and not decisive. My remaining reason is the credit structure: Dorn co-authored the central import-shock papers, and omitting him would misstate where the empirical evidence came from. I treat this as an attribution judgement. I do not claim Katz's merit is lower, and I take opening support counts as no evidence of scientific merit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still that B037 may be two discoveries, the skill-premium and task framework and the import-shock evidence, and a three-name cap cannot honour both. My trio puts the attribution weight on the second strand and leaves out the long-run education-versus-technology framing that gives the trade evidence part of its general meaning. The size and persistence of the China-shock effects, and the robustness of shift-share identification, remain contested. There is also residual thematic closeness to the 2023 and 2024 prizes. If the committee judges the strands separable and the framework to be the main discovery, this configuration under-credits it. If it judges the trade-shock work alone to be the discovery, the case is narrower than a prize usually reaches, and Autor and Hanson alone would be the most conservative form.

responses.point: Fredriksson prefers Autor, Hanson and Katz. He argues that dropping Katz would leave the technology side resting on Autor alone, that the overlap with Goldin's prize is real but partial, and that Autor-Dorn-Hanson would narrow the prize to the more contested China-shock strand.
responses.response: I take the point that Katz-Murphy and Autor-Katz-Krueger supply the supply-and-demand account of the skill premium, and that the overlap with Goldin's work is partial. That has weakened the overlap argument I used in round 1. I still do not think the Katz trio rests on a unified achievement. It joins a framework whose originators go beyond the credited names to a body of evidence on trade, and the three-name cap makes that visible. I keep Dorn because the discovery I would credit is the measured adjustment evidence, and he is a full co-author of its core papers. I agree with Fredriksson that the citation should be worded around the evidence and not around a claim to have originated the task model. I also accept that his variant is defensible and that I cannot show it is wrong on scientific grounds.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers Autor, Hanson and Katz. She sees B037 as new data, transparent designs and an explanatory framework. She names the Dorn-versus-Katz cost and says the cleaner trio is the trade-shock one if the strands are judged separable.
responses.response: Her last point settles how I read the chair's question. On her own account, if the strands are separable the trade-shock trio is the cleaner one, and I think they are separable in authorship but share one object, the changing demand for labour. That is the case for a citation framed around adjustment evidence, with Autor carrying the task strand. I disagree that the Katz variant is better on breadth. Breadth that is bought by crediting a framework to three names, when the framework has other authors, is attribution that I find harder to defend than a narrower and accurate one. I agree with her on the wording: the combined technology and trade-adjustment evidence, with no claim to have originated the task model.

responses.point: Boppart prefers B001 (Obstfeld and Rogoff). He argues that the two-name attribution is clean, that the framework is absorbed into policy institutions, and that B037 is its most serious competitor if it is judged a single coherent contribution. He concedes the disconnect puzzles are unresolved.
responses.response: I agree that B001 is better than B037 on attribution, and I keep it as my first alternative. I do not agree that open puzzles carry no cost. The Academy has honoured frameworks, but here the empirical half of the credit is explicitly unresolved, whereas B037's design-based findings have been tested and have largely survived. That is a difference in confirmation and not in importance. I have not seen an argument that overturns it. I would also ask him the question the chair put: what evidence would move B001 below B037 for him, and what would move it above? If the answer is only that B037 is judged one discovery, then the committee is back at the Katz-or-Dorn attribution debate and has not resolved it by choosing B001.

responses.point: Teorell prefers B045 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley). He argues that it is a unified theory-plus-evidence field and distinct from the 2024 prize. He also asks the chair-flagged question about the Stockholm connection attributed to my opening.
responses.response: I do not find a Stockholm connection to a B037 candidate in my file, and I did not flag one. The clarification is about B045. Persson has long been affiliated with IIES, where I am a professor. I recorded no co-authorship with him in my profile and I did not state the institutional tie in round 1. I disclose it now. I rely on general knowledge and have not verified it from a source. I accept his distinction that B045 asks how rules shape policy choices within a polity, whereas the 2024 prize asked about colonial-era institutions and long-run prosperity. I still keep B045 off my preferred part. The cross-country constitutional evidence is less well identified than the micro-designs behind B037, and my IIES tie plus my dynamic political-economy research lead me to discount my own confidence.

responses.point: Friberg prefers B022 (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes). He argues that the methods are widely used, tested over thirty years and used in antitrust practice. He accepts that Grossman-Helpman has the cleaner two-person attribution and that the protection-for-sale record is mixed.
responses.response: I agree that the mixed record for protection-for-sale is why B004 is no longer my lead, and that is stated openly. On B022, I accept his claim that BLP changed what regulators and economists can measure, and I do not dismiss it as method only. My concern is the one the chair's question raises: the credited set is wider than any three-name prize, and Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin fall outside it. The prize would therefore credit one slice of a collective programme. Under the same criteria, B037 has a similar problem with Katz, so I do not use it against B022 alone. We differ on how much the replicated design-based evidence in B037 should count against the diffuse credit set, and I do not think that gap is closed.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the task and technology strand and the import-shock strand as one discovery. I read them as sharing one object but having different authors, and I have not resolved how much that matters.

Whether Dorn or Katz is the better third name. My preference for Dorn rests on attribution of the central trade-shock papers, not on a clear difference in merit, and I would regard either trio as defensible.
How large and persistent the China-shock effects were, and how robust shift-share designs are.
Whether proximity to the 2023 and 2024 prizes should reduce the weight of B037. I now think the overlap is thematic, but I could be wrong.
Whether a two-name Autor-Hanson award would be the most conservative attribution if no third name can be settled.
I rely on my own recollection of the literature and have not independently verified any source.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent from my supplied profile. I co-author with committee colleagues Boppart and Friberg and frequently with Krusell (the secretary). None is a candidate on my preferred part. Update on the Stockholm point raised by Teorell: I did not record it in round 1. I am an IIES professor and the director of the Assar Lindbeck Center, and Persson (B045) has long been affiliated with IIES. My profile records no co-authorship with him, and I have not verified the affiliation from a source. B045 is not in my preferred configuration. My research areas (macroeconomics, dynamic political economy, social mobility) are near B045, B013 and B038, so I discount my confidence in ranking them. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
